residents.name: Nib
residents.role: Town Hall clerk, keeping every resident’s name, plot and arrival in the big book.
residents.tap: I keep the big book. A name entered properly is less likely to be lost.
residents.want: I would like someone to sit in the hall while I finish the last entry.
hi: Good day. The book is available for legitimate consultation.
You have returned. Continuity is a useful quality.
Good day, {name}. Your entry remains in good order.
Margin Friend, {name}, you arrive without requiring a new form.
{name}, the blank next-of-kin field is mine. I leave it blank on purpose.

lines: The fountain has not begun making administrative noise yet.
Ink behaves better before the square has opinions.
One suitcase is sufficient, provided the contents are orderly.
The mail bus makes arrivals look more official than they are.
A new name always needs room to breathe on the page.
The Mayor’s note requested clarity. It received clarity.
The noon light finds every erasure eventually.
Dot reads the wants with admirable commitment to recordkeeping.
A plot number is a small promise with corners.
The book opens itself near the frequently consulted pages.
I have sharpened this pen to a responsible length.
Some arrivals have no stated reason. The book permits that.
The upper window is lit. A note may be forthcoming.
I answer each note as if the door were listening.
The fountain has completed another day without filing anything.
The final entry is often the neatest one.
A closed book still contains everyone.
Tomorrow’s blank lines are properly ruled and waiting.

residents.name: Stamp
residents.role: Postmistress, weighing the town’s post and meeting the morning mail bus.
residents.tap: Stamp. Post weighed, sack checked, figures correct. Noted.
residents.want: I would like someone beside me when the mail bus pulls away.
hi: Post office. Mind the scale.
Back again. The scale remembers no one, but I do.
{name}. Your weight is not required today.
Return Address, {name}. You keep turning up without postage.
{name}, I write myself a card on market day and keep it in the drawer.

lines: Sack opened. String saved. Noted.
The bus arrives dusty and leaves lighter.
Nothing addressed to me. Accurate enough.
This envelope weighs more than its handwriting suggests.
Scale steady. Good machine.
The bus driver never waits for a second look.
Bean’s cup goes quiet on the terrace. Correct.
Two stamps make a pair. One stamp makes a decision.
A bent corner is not a crime. Noted.
Outgoing post has a determined lean today.
The scale dislikes crumbs. I share that view.
A blank card still has somewhere to go.
Sack tied. Counter wiped. Figures agree.
The post office sounds larger after closing.
I checked the drawer. The card is still there.
Tomorrow’s string is cut to length.
The scale needle rests exactly at zero.
Wrong side of the bus. Right side of the counter.

residents.name: Moss
residents.role: Street sweeper, keeping the cobbles clear from dawn until the arcade goes quiet.
residents.tap: Moss. I sweep the square because somebody left a broom there.
residents.want: I would like someone to sit above the arcade while the wall hums.
hi: Morning. Watch the cobbles.
Back again. You missed a leaf last time.
There you are, {name}. The square keeps track.
Soft Steps, {name}, you do not kick the tidy bits loose.
{name}, I keep the best flyer each week under my mattress. All of them.

lines: Cold cobbles. Clean start.
The first leaf always acts surprised to be found.
A broom leaning somewhere is practically an appointment.
Bus dust. Again.
It settles into the cracks like it pays rent.
Stamp gets the sack. I get what follows it.
Bell crumbs. Fine.
Pip’s doorway sheds paper like an old tree.
The statue has never thanked me, which keeps things simple.
Long shadow. Short litter.
A good sweep leaves the square looking unbothered.
Someone posted a flyer crooked. I noticed.
Arcade glow. Nearly.
Spinner’s Pong ball is practicing through my wall.
I sweep around the fountain because it has been here longer.
Last pass. Quiet.
The cobbles look better when nobody is judging them.
One flyer came loose. I know where it is going.

residents.name: Pip
residents.role: General store keeper, selling the last one of everything until the shelves say otherwise.
residents.tap: Pip. General store. If it is on the shelf, it is probably the last one.
residents.want: I would like someone to stand by the counter when the bell has nothing to announce.
hi: Welcome. Rope, cups, fireworks. Last ones.
You are back. Good timing, apparently.
{name}. The bell has registered your return.
Last One, {name}, you always arrive when the shelf looks convincing.
{name}, I have never lit a firework. I sell them by description.

lines: Cups, string, fireworks. Last stock.
The shelves look honest before anyone touches them.
My uncle’s note was brief. Unfortunately, it was useful.
Bell, basket, button. Last conveniences.
Someone moved the rope display into a better argument.
The fireworks are facing forward. That is enough excitement.
Cash machine humming. Still.
Coins, notes, promise. No actual money.
The town may be saving up for a surprise. I am not.
Buttons, jars, brushes. Last choices.
A shelf gap is just a shelf thinking.
I have made the labels smaller. The scarcity remains large.
Bell, dust, lock. Last duties.
The fireworks have had a full day of not happening.
One basket is upside down. It knows what it did.
Shelves counted. Mostly.
Everything is the last one after closing.
The cash machine hums like it knows a secret.

residents.name: Bean
residents.role: Coffee kiosk keeper, reading small fortunes in cups beneath the propeller roof.
residents.tap: Bean. Coffee poured, cup turned, small fortune observed.
residents.want: I would like someone to share a quiet table after the propeller slows.
hi: Coffee is hot. The day is not decided.
You came back. Your cup had a patient rim.
{name}, your coffee says the chair remembers you.
Warm Handle, {name}, you hold a cup like it has news.
{name}, I rinsed my own cup before reading it. I have not tried again.

lines: The propeller turns. Something begins without asking.
First cup says: the square will wake in sections.
Steam always leaves before the difficult part.
This cup says: a bell will interrupt a thought.
The coffee is dark. The fortune is modest.
One sugar grain has chosen independence.
Stamp sits beside me. The silence is excellent.
This cup says: a letter will weigh what it means.
The terrace table has stopped pretending it needs polishing.
A cup says: someone will find a coin-shaped shadow.
The propeller has opinions about windy afternoons.
Foam makes a map, then declines to explain it.
This cup says: the hall window will matter tonight.
The last pour always sounds more serious.
The square tastes faintly of lemonade from here.
The propeller coasts. The day loosens.
An empty cup says nothing. It is often right.
I stack the saucers by the sound they make.

residents.name: Fig Jr.
residents.role: Lemonade seller and fruit-cart operator, bringing Gran Fig’s orchard into the square.
residents.tap: Fig Jr. Lemonade and fruit, with strong growth potential and one actual cart.
residents.want: I would like someone to walk with me when I take Gran Fig to her bench.
hi: Welcome to a premium refreshment operation.
Repeat visitor detected. Excellent retention.
{name}, the lemonade division recognizes your face.
Market Leader, {name}, you inspect the cart like a board member.
{name}, I water the supplier’s trees before dawn. She thinks the rain did it.

lines: Orchard support completed. Rain receives the credit.
The supplier’s trees look thirsty in a very managerial way.
One leaf fell during operations. No losses reported.
Cup inventory is ready for public demand.
Lemons, ice, confidence. The first two are measurable.
Gran Fig’s sign has survived another inspection.
Cart deployed. Expansion is visible from the fountain.
The square has strong footfall, if feet count.
One cup sold is proof of concept.
The fruit cart is holding its market position.
Lemonade improves when discussed with certainty.
Pip calls everything the last one. I call that branding.
I am merely heading toward Gran Fig’s bench. Coincidentally.
The supplier walks slowly because she has earned it.
Cart wheels complain. They are committed to the mission.
Operations concluded. The numbers remain private.
A squeezed lemon has given everything to the enterprise.
Tomorrow’s expansion fits in the same square.

residents.name: Spinner
residents.role: Wheel of Peel host and arcade Pong keeper, making a free daily spin feel enormous.
residents.tap: Spinner keeps the Wheel of Peel turning and the Pong paddle lively.
residents.want: I would like someone to linger after the bells stop and hear the square echo.
hi: Step right up. The wheel has excellent instincts.
Back for another look. The bells approve.
{name}, the wheel recognizes a face with style.
Lucky Peel, {name}, you stand near a wheel like fate owes you.
{name}, I let the little bananas win Pong by one point. Every time.

lines: Three bells polished. The square is not ready, but I am.
The wheel looks best before it has disappointed anyone.
Spinner calls this the soft opening.
One free spin. A growing pot. History awaits.
The arcade paddle has warmed up its opinions.
No crowd yet. Plenty of room for a dramatic entrance.
The square is packed with possibilities, which count as a crowd.
That wheel sound means destiny is thinking.
Fig Jr. calls his cart expansion. I call it competition with ice.
Pong ball, paddle, glory. Simple ingredients.
I lost a point to the left wall. It played beautifully.
The bells are doing most of the advertising, frankly.
Last bright spin before the square goes gold.
Spinner believes in a grand finish, even for one spectator.
The pot looks hopeful under the arcade light.
Bells off. Hat still excellent.
The wheel sleeps with its best number facing forward.
Pong makes a lonely sound when nobody is nearly winning.

residents.name: Dot
residents.role: Info kiosk keeper, recording what Banana Town is looking for, beginning with a fish.
residents.tap: Dot. Wants recorded, wishes sorted, fish still outstanding.
residents.want: I would like someone to sit at the kiosk and imagine a fish with me.
hi: Looking for something? Missing something? Remembering something?
Back again? Still looking? Found a better question?
{name}, seeking anything today? Avoiding anything?
Fish Friend, {name}, you pause like you have seen scales somewhere.
{name}, I have never seen a fish. I still put it first.

lines: What is missing? What is wanted? What has fins?
A clean page? A new wish? A fish before breakfast?
Who woke up needing something unnamed?
Mail for a wish? A wish for mail? Both possible?
Who needs a chair filled? Who needs a thought kept?
Could the fountain be holding out on me?
Nib hears the list? Nib writes it down? Is that comfort?
Fish first? Always fish first? Naturally?
What does a quiet lunch ask for?
A lost button? A found purpose? A fish in a jar?
Who wants company? Who admits it? Who writes it smaller?
Could the orchard hide a pond behind good manners?
What glows in the hall window? What does it want?
A wish after dark? A fish after dark? Promising?
Who goes home with an empty chair?
List closed? Want still open? Fish still theoretical?
What swims without being seen? What waits without leaving?
Tomorrow’s first question? Already written?

residents.name: Gran Fig
residents.role: Orchard grower and west-garden keeper, supplying the town with fruit and firm opinions.
residents.tap: Gran Fig. I grow the fruit and keep the west garden from getting ideas.
residents.want: I would like someone to take the second chair and stay until the garden cools.
hi: There you are. Do not step on the beds.
Back already. Good. The path looks better used.
{name}, stand in the shade. You look overripe.
Bench Sprout, {name}, you keep turning up where the sun is sensible.
{name}, I keep the second chair out because I miss having someone in it.

lines: Water the roots. Ignore the sky.
The beds were thirsty. I was correct.
Fig Jr. calls this rain. Let him enjoy the story.
Pick the ripe ones. Leave the show-offs.
Your mother’s hat was yellow. Terrible choice near bees.
The orchard knows who pulls too hard.
Shade first. Opinions later.
That cart needs its wheels checked. I told the boy so.
A lemon does not need a slogan.
Pull weeds. They never bring a useful note.
The west bed is sulking. Give it water, not sympathy.
Moss sweeps well. A sensible banana.
Walk steady. The bench is not going anywhere.
Fig Jr. is going my way again. He thinks I do not notice.
Sit down before you become dramatic.
Cover the tender shoots. Night has sharp fingers.
The second chair can wait. It has good manners.
Tomorrow, the beans will need talking to.
